3. Executive Summary

The Predictive RF-Wild (PRW-Wild) platform is an integrated cyber-physical wildlife monitoring, early-warning, and digital-twin architecture designed to detect wildlife approaching agricultural perimeter boundaries before physical fence breaches occur. The system bridges physical field-deployable IoT sensing hardware with a high-fidelity WebGL 3D virtual environment running in real time.

This audit establishes the actual ground-truth implementation of the project as of November 10, 2026:

  • Complete Three-Layer Sensing Pipeline: Outer RF sensing corridor (Layer 1, X = 45m to 70m), middle physical multi-modal sensor network (Layer 2, X = 70m to 85m), and inner optical camera surveillance (Layer 3, X = 85m to 100m) terminating at the perimeter boundary fence at X = 100.0m.
  • Dual Physical Microcontroller Architecture: Node A (ESP32-WROOM-32 Remote Sensor Acquisition Node) acquires HC-SR501 PIR motion, I2S INMP441 acoustic telemetry, and conditioned piezoelectric vibration signals, transmitting periodic packets over 433.92 MHz LoRa. Node B (ESP32-WROOM-32 LED Gateway) receives LoRa telemetry, validates sequence integrity, actuates six discrete physical LEDs (with 2 kΩ ballast resistors), and streams machine-readable telemetry over USB Serial (CP2102 @ 115200 baud) to the host computer.
  • Dual Hardware Manifest Ground Truth: The audit resolved a critical distinction between the Physical Bench Setup (dual ESP32-WROOM-32 nodes documented in hardware/wiring_manifest_actual.json) and the Interactive 3D Hardware Lab Workbench (single-board ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 v1.1 with 11 3D Catmull-Rom tube cables documented in hardware/wiring_manifest.json).
  • Rigorous Electrical Safety Gate: Raw piezoelectric discs generate destructive transient spikes from -30V to +50V. The firmware enforces a compile-time fail-closed safety gate (PIEZO_CIRCUIT_VERIFIED=0) that completely suppresses ADC sampling until dual Schottky (BAT54S) clamping and resistive attenuation are confirmed.
  • 100% Automated Regression Pass Rate: The test suite comprises 139 collected items, 139 passed, 0 failed in 21.90 seconds across 18 test modules, verifying configuration schemas, mathematical geometry, sensor fusion, boids flocking, quaternion locomotion physics, state leakage isolation, and physical telemetry parsing.
  • Immersive 3D Digital Twin: Built on Three.js with an exact 120 × 120 analytical elevation grid (280m × 260m terrain), 1200m ground skirt, rigged Asian Elephant production GLB (5.65MB), 16 modeled Indian wildlife species, 13 PBR botanical models, and nine camera viewpoints.

4. Project Objectives

The core engineering objective of PRW-Wild is to resolve the fundamental trade-off in remote wildlife monitoring between detection range, response lead time, false-alarm rate, and electrical power consumption:

  1. Precursor Detection via Non-Line-of-Sight Sensing: Detect large mammals (specifically Asian Elephants, Elephas maximus) 30 to 55 metres prior to fence arrival using RF and physical sensor disturbance signatures.
  2. Power Conservation via Multi-Modal Camera Gating: Continuous operation of optical pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) cameras and high-power deep neural network vision models exhausts solar/battery reserves. PRW-Wild gates camera activation so that optical surveillance is powered only when fused multi-sensor confidence exceeds calibrated threat thresholds, achieving >80% energy savings.
  3. False-Alarm Suppression through Multi-Sensor Corroboration: Eliminates single-sensor nuisance triggers (e.g. wind-induced foliage movement or small rodents) by requiring cross-corroboration between PIR pyroelectric signals, seismic acoustic RMS counts, and RF Doppler variations.
  4. Bi-Directional Cyber-Physical Twinning: Provide human rangers and forest authorities with an intuitive, real-time 3D tactical interface reflecting physical sensor states while isolating digital twin state mutations from hardware faults.

5. System Overview

PRW-Wild executes a continuous cyber-physical control loop structured into five primary stages:

Complete System Workflow:
Wildlife Movement in Forest Habitat (X < 100m) → Physical & Synthetic Multi-Layer Sensing Infrastructure → ESP32-A Edge Acquisition & LoRa Packetization → 433.92 MHz Wireless Link → ESP32-B Gateway & Six-LED Actuation → USB-UART Host Ingestion (COM7 @ 115200 baud) → Python Backend Sensor Fusion & Heuristic Risk Engine → REST API & Three.js WebGL Digital Twin Visualization → Tactical Operator Monitoring & Deterrent Dispatch.

The system maintains strict architectural boundaries between the Physical Hardware Domain (microcontrollers, radios, sensors, and LEDs) and the Digital Twin Simulation Domain (virtual boids, 3D assets, and synthetic scenario runners). Physical hardware telemetry is ingested asynchronously and displayed in dedicated dashboard panels, but never overwrites or corrupts the simulated digital twin state (verified by tests/test_leakage.py).

7. Three-Layer Wildlife Monitoring Architecture

The core detection topology is structured into three concentric sensing envelopes positioned in the western forest zone approaching the boundary fence at X = 100.0m.

Figure 7.1: Three-Layer Sensing Topology, Spatial Boundaries, and Habitat Geography.

7.1 Layer 1 — Outer Sensing Layer (X = 45m to 70m)

  • Concept & Visual Identity: Broad-area precursor detection envelope rendered as a glowing cyan mesh (#00f0ff).
  • Spatial Boundaries: Geometry mesh spans X = 45.0m to 70.0m (width: 25.0m, length: 196.0m along North-South axis). Simulation transition logic registers occupancy when an animal's X coordinate satisfies 45.0m <= X <= 100.0m.
  • Implementation Ground Truth: In the active software simulation, Layer 1 is modeled via stochastic observation models (sensor_models.py, detection probability 0.85, noise std 0.15). Real physical Wi-Fi CSI subcarrier extraction is NOT implemented; csi_replay.py is an interface stub. Physical RF communication uses LoRa (Ai-Thinker RA-02 SX1278 @ 433.92 MHz), which must not be confused with Wi-Fi CSI sensing.

7.2 Layer 2 — Middle Physical Sensor Layer (X = 70m to 85m)

  • Concept & Visual Identity: Multi-modal physical ground-truth confirmation corridor rendered as a glowing amber mesh (#f59e0b).
  • Spatial Boundaries: Geometry mesh spans X = 70.0m to 85.0m (width: 15.0m, length: 196.0m). Simulation transition logic triggers when 70.0m <= X <= 100.0m.
  • Hardware Implementation: Physical sensing is executed by the ESP32-A Sensor Node acquiring three complementary modalities:
    1. HC-SR501 PIR Sensor: Pyroelectric infrared detecting thermal body signatures on GPIO32.
    2. INMP441 MEMS Microphone: High-bandwidth I2S digital acoustic monitoring on GPIO25 (BCLK), GPIO33 (WS), GPIO34 (SD).
    3. Piezoelectric Geophone Disc: Ground seismic vibration monitoring on GPIO35 (ADC1_CH7, currently gated).
  • Telemetry & Actuation: Transmitted via 433.92 MHz LoRa to the ESP32-B Gateway, which illuminates physical LEDs 1, 2, 3, and 6 in real time.

7.3 Layer 3 — Inner Camera Surveillance Layer (X = 85m to 100m)

  • Concept & Visual Identity: Immediate proximity visual confirmation zone rendered as a violet frustum envelope (#a855f7).
  • Spatial Boundaries: Geometry mesh spans X = 85.0m to 100.0m (width: 15.0m, length: 196.0m). Transition triggers when 85.0m <= X <= 100.0m.
  • Virtual Camera Implementation: A virtual optical camera (CAM_01) mounted on a 6m mast at coordinate (100.0, 100.0) facing West (orientation: 270°) with a 55° horizontal field of view. When triggered, it renders a picture-in-picture optical viewfinder with automated target bounding-box calculation and YOLOv8 deep learning inference.
  • Physical Camera Status: The commercial Xiaomi 360° Home Security Camera 2K is maintained as an external consumer IoT device accessed via the Xiaomi Home mobile app. It is NOT integrated into the Python backend or web UI via RTSP/ONVIF.

8. Spatial Boundaries and Sensor Coverage

The audit revealed an essential operational characteristic regarding the mathematical definition of layer boundaries in the codebase:

Boundary Discrepancy & Nested Logic Analysis

In src/prw_wild/web/static/app.js, the 3D visual rendering meshes and the programmatic event-detection state machine use complementary but distinct boundary representations:

LayerVisual 3D Mesh BandMesh Center & DimensionsLogical Event Transition RegionBehavioral Rationale
Layer 1 (Outer) 45.0m to 70.0m Center X = 57.5m, Width = 25m X >= 45.0m && X <= 100.0m Visual mesh highlights the outer precursor zone; logic treats L1 as active continuously as animal approaches fence.
Layer 2 (Middle) 70.0m to 85.0m Center X = 77.5m, Width = 15m X >= 70.0m && X <= 100.0m Visual mesh indicates the physical sensor deployment zone; logic maintains L2 alert state once penetrated.
Layer 3 (Inner) 85.0m to 100.0m Center X = 92.5m, Width = 15m X >= 85.0m && X <= 100.0m Visual frustum covers camera line of sight; terminates exactly at perimeter fence (X = 100.0m).
Forensic Boundary Finding:
The three visual meshes are contiguous and non-overlapping (45–70m, 70–85m, 85–100m). However, the underlying detection logic in checkSimulationLayerTransitions is nested and cumulative: an animal at X = 90.0m activates L1, L2, and L3 simultaneously. When retreating, layers deactivate in the strict reverse order: L3 EXIT at X < 85m, L2 EXIT at X < 70m, and L1 EXIT at X < 45m.

10. ESP32-A — Sensor Acquisition Node

The ESP32-A firmware (firmware/ESP32_A_Sensor_Node/ESP32_A_Sensor_Node.ino, 380 lines) runs an autonomous acquisition and packetization loop on the remote sensing node.

Initialization Sequence & Sensor Drivers

  1. Serial & Entropy Initialization: Configures Serial at 115200 baud; generates a cryptographically random 32-bit boot session ID (esp_random()).
  2. ADC Configuration: Configures 12-bit resolution (analogReadResolution(12)) and 11 dB attenuation (ADC_11db) on GPIO35 (ADC1_CH7).
  3. I2S Acoustic Sampling (INMP441): Initializes the I2S driver on BCLK=GPIO25, WS=GPIO33, SD=GPIO34. Configures 16 kHz sample rate, 24-bit data in 32-bit slot, mono Left channel.
  4. LoRa Transceiver Setup: Initializes SPI bus (SCK=18, MISO=19, MOSI=23, CS=27, RST=14, DIO0=26) at 433.92 MHz, SF7, BW 125 kHz, CR 4/5, sync word 0x12, Tx power 2 dBm, and hardware CRC enabled.

Telemetry Frame Generation

Every 700 ms, the node formats and transmits an ASCII telemetry frame matching the PW1 specification: 

PW1|TEL|A|<bootIdHex>|<seq>|<uptimeMs>|<flags>|<pirRaw>|<piezoP2P>|<micRms>|<pirActive>|<piezoActive>|<micActive>

Hardware Status Flags Bitfield

BitMaskFlag NameOperational Condition
00x01PIR_WARMED_UPActive when node uptime exceeds 45,000 ms (pyroelectric baseline stabilized)
10x02PIEZO_CIRCUIT_VERIFIEDReflects compile-time safety gate; false (0) by default to prevent ADC destruction
20x04INMP441_OPERATIONALTrue when I2S driver returns non-zero valid audio buffers
30x08PIEZO_ADC_VALIDTrue when ADC conversions show no saturation faults
40x10MIC_ACOUSTIC_VALIDTrue when microphone frame exhibits normal acoustic variance

11. ESP32-B — LoRa Receiver, Six-LED Controller and USB Gateway

The ESP32-B firmware (firmware/ESP32_B_LED_Gateway/ESP32_B_LED_Gateway.ino, 420 lines) serves as the cyber-physical bridge connecting the remote RF sensor network to the host computer.

Six-LED Actuation Mapping

IndicatorGPIO PinElectrical DriveFunctional Activation Condition
LED 1 (PIR)GPIO 322 kΩ resistor (~0.60 mA)Illuminates when Node-A PIR is warmed up and detects thermal motion
LED 2 (Piezo)GPIO 332 kΩ resistor (~0.60 mA)Illuminates when Piezo is verified and peak-to-peak vibration exceeds threshold
LED 3 (Mic)GPIO 252 kΩ resistor (~0.60 mA)Illuminates when INMP441 digital RMS counts exceed calibrated threshold
LED 4 (Heartbeat)GPIO 132 kΩ resistor (~0.60 mA)Steady ON while Node-A packets arrive within 2200 ms timeout; OFF when stale
LED 5 (LoRa Pulse)GPIO 212 kΩ resistor (~0.60 mA)Flashes for exactly 120 ms upon receipt of every valid Node-A LoRa frame
LED 6 (Alert)GPIO 222 kΩ resistor (~0.60 mA)Logical OR combination: illuminates if PIR || Piezo || Mic is active
Prohibited GPIO Pin Warning (ESP32-WROOM-32):
GPIO 34 and GPIO 35 are strictly input-only on classic ESP32 microcontrollers. They do not possess internal output driver transistors. Configuring GPIO34 or GPIO35 with pinMode(pin, OUTPUT) fails silently and will never drive an LED. The verified firmware strictly utilizes GPIOs 32, 33, 25, 13, 21, and 22 for all outputs.

Serial Telemetry Output to Python Host

Upon receiving and validating each packet, ESP32-B appends hardware RF channel diagnostics (RSSI and SNR) and streams an ASCII line over USB UART: 

PW1|TEL_USB|B|<bootIdHex>|<seq>|<uptimeMs>|<flags>|<pirRaw>|<piezoP2P>|<micRms>|<pirActive>|<piezoActive>|<micActive>|<rssi>|<snr>

18 & 19. Frontend Architecture and 3D Digital Twin Visualization

The digital twin frontend is rendered via Three.js (WebGL) inside modern web browsers. It provides an interactive 3D representation of the wildlife sanctuary, terrain elevation, multi-agent boids, and cyber-physical hardware status.

Core Frontend Modules

  • Unified 120 × 120 Terrain Plane: A single continuous THREE.PlaneGeometry(280, 260, 120, 120) spanning 280m East-West and 260m North-South. The elevation of every vertex is calculated analytically via getTerrainElevation(x, z) to eradicate black void gaps and visual seams.
  • 1200m Horizon Ground Skirt: A large perimeter mesh (1200m × 1200m) surrounding the core terrain to ensure horizon continuity across all camera pitch angles.
  • PUBG-Style Tactical Inspection HUD: High-contrast military-grade UI featuring tactical corner brackets, central crosshair reticle, real-time coordinate stamp, and dedicated fullscreen toggle.
  • 3D Hardware Lab Workbench: An interactive secondary 3D scene rendering the ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 v1.1 microcontroller, sensor daughterboards, and 11 individual 3D Catmull-Rom TubeGeometry connecting wires with raycast pin inspection.

Elephant Locomotion Physics & Quaternion Heading Lock

The rigged production Asian Elephant model (asian_elephant_production.glb, 5.65MB) implements a dedicated quaternion-based orientation controller (tools/apply_quaternion_locomotion_controller.py and tests/test_elephant_locomotion.py). Key locomotion algorithms include:

  • Forward Vector Alignment: Eliminates model inversion by locking heading to velocity vector v = (Δx, Δz). When Δx > 0, the elephant faces East toward the fence.
  • Zero-Velocity Heading Preservation: When animal speed drops below 0.0001 m/s, the orientation controller latches the previous valid quaternion, preventing erratic spinning during pauses.
  • Dynamic Leg Animation Blending: Animation playback speed scales dynamically with ground velocity, achieving realistic footfall cadence without foot-sliding artifacts.

22 & 23. Event Pipeline and Multi-Factor Risk Assessment

Spatial Layer Transition Invariant

PRW-Wild enforces a strict event ordering invariant for all wildlife crossing events: 

APPROACH (West to East):   L1 ENTER (X=45m) → L2 ENTER (X=70m) → L3 ENTER (X=85m) → PERIMETER BREACH (X=100m)
RETREAT  (East to West):   L3 EXIT  (X<85m) → L2 EXIT  (X<70m) → L1 EXIT  (X<45m)

Heuristic Multi-Factor Risk Calculation

The risk assessment engine (src/prw_wild/risk_engine.py) combines four independent evidential components into a composite threat score R in [0, 1]:

R = wboundary · Cboundary + weta · Ceta + wconf · Cconf + wtrack · Ctrack

ComponentConfiguration WeightMathematical FormulationPhysical Significance
Boundary Proximity (Cboundary)wboundary = 0.351.0 - min(1.0, dfence / 50.0)Proximity to perimeter fence at X = 100m
Time-to-Arrival (Ceta)weta = 0.25max(0.0, 1.0 - ETA / 60.0)Extrapolated arrival lead time based on velocity raycast
Fused Sensor Confidence (Cconf)wconf = 0.25Evidential multi-sensor weighted sumCorroborated certainty across RF, PIR, and acoustic channels
Track Quality (Ctrack)wtrack = 0.15Kalman filter observation count & covarianceStatistical stability of the estimated motion vector

Hysteresis State Machine

To prevent rapid oscillating alerts (chatter) when animals hover near threshold boundaries, the engine applies an asymmetric hysteresis band of ±0.05:

  • Transition to WATCH: Risk score exceeds 0.35 (drops back to LOW only if score falls below 0.30).
  • Transition to HIGH: Risk score exceeds 0.60 (drops back to WATCH only if score falls below 0.55).
  • Camera Trigger: Camera activates when risk level reaches HIGH or fused confidence exceeds 0.55).

24. Optical Camera Surveillance Layer & YOLOv8 Inference

Layer 3 optical surveillance provides visual target confirmation. The system implements a two-tier architecture:

  1. Virtual Surveillance Camera (CAM_01): Mounted at coordinates (100.0, 100.0, 6.0) with an optical field-of-view of 55°. Renders real-time viewport frames into a hidden canvas buffer.
  2. ONNX Deep Learning Vision Engine: The detector (src/prw_wild/vision/detector.py) executes a forward pass of yolov8n.onnx (12.8MB) via the ONNX Runtime engine. It processes 640 × 640 letterboxed RGB images, extracts bounding boxes, and outputs raw confidence scores for wildlife detection.
  3. Spatial Morphological Fallback: If neural inference fails or model confidence is marginal, the engine falls back to a deterministic OpenCV-style morphological contour detector, ensuring fail-safe target tracking.
Physical Camera Integration Boundary:
The physical Xiaomi 360° Home Security Camera 2K is documented in project records as an independent bench surveillance feed. It is managed entirely via the proprietary Xiaomi Home mobile application. It has no local RTSP, ONVIF, or WebRTC streaming pipeline integrated into the web dashboard or backend server.

Electrical & Power Architecture

  • Common Ground Bus: ESP32-A, RA-02, INMP441, HC-SR501, and Piezo transducer share a unified ground plane to prevent floating voltage references.
  • Voltage Domain Integrity: INMP441 and RA-02 are strictly powered from the regulated 3.3V rail. HC-SR501 is supplied from the 5V rail; its onboard 7133-1 LDO outputs a 3.3V logic level safely compatible with ESP32 GPIOs.
  • ADC Protection: Unconditioned piezoelectric transducers produce transient spikes up to +50V, exceeding the ESP32 absolute maximum rating (3.6V). The BAT54S dual Schottky pair clamps input voltage within -0.2V to +3.5V.

Security, Reliability and Failure Management

  • Fail-Closed Piezoelectric Safety Gate: Firmware strictly enforces PIEZO_CIRCUIT_VERIFIED=0 at compile time. Sampling is physically disabled until an electrical protection circuit (BAT54S) is confirmed, protecting ADC1_CH7 from destructive over-voltage spikes.
  • Zero Ground-Truth State Leakage: Verified by tests/test_leakage.py. Physical telemetry ingested via LoraSerialBridge is routed strictly to hardware monitoring state and cannot mutate or bias the simulated digital twin coordinates.
  • Cascading Node Dependency (A_OFF_FORCES_B_OFF): If Node A (remote sensor acquisition) is powered down, Node B (LED gateway) automatically cascades to OFF. Node B cannot be enabled while Node A is inactive, eliminating phantom alerting.
  • Monotonic Sequence Tracking & Stale Rejection: ESP32-B validates incoming packet sequence numbers against active boot session IDs. Duplicate packets (delta = 0) and stale/out-of-order packets (delta < 0) are safely acknowledged but rejected from actuator processing.
  • Emergency Stop Interlock: Accessible via UI button, REST API (POST /api/hardware/emergency_stop), or serial command (PW1|EMERGENCY_STOP). Immediately forces all 6 physical LEDs LOW and halts all hardware actuation.

33 & 34. Limitations, Technical Gaps and Engineering Roadmap

Identified Technical Limitations & Inconsistencies

  1. Synthetic Nature of Wi-Fi CSI in Current Codebase: While Layer 1 is designated conceptually as Wi-Fi CSI disturbance sensing, no physical CSI collection pipeline exists in production. The file csi_replay.py is strictly an abstract interface stub. Layer 1 detections in the digital twin are generated by stochastic simulation models.
  2. Uncalibrated Piezoelectric Circuitry: Due to the destructive voltage spike potential of raw piezoelectric transducers (-30V to +50V), the firmware safety gate (PIEZO_CIRCUIT_VERIFIED=0) correctly keeps seismic sampling disabled. Field detection distance cannot be claimed until a conditioned analog front-end (Schottky clamping + DC bias + operational amplifier) is constructed.
  3. Physical Camera Streaming Disconnect: The Xiaomi 360° Home Security Camera 2K operates solely through the proprietary Xiaomi Home smartphone app. It lacks an RTSP/ONVIF local bridge to pipe live H.264 video into the browser dashboard.
  4. Digital RMS Counts vs Absolute SPL: The INMP441 microphone records raw digital RMS counts (e.g. 32,000 counts) rather than calibrated Sound Pressure Levels (dB SPL). Acoustic calibration against a Class 1 sound level meter has not been performed.
  5. Dual Hardware Manifest Coexistence: The presence of wiring_manifest.json (ESP32-S3 virtual lab) and wiring_manifest_actual.json (dual ESP32-WROOM-32 bench) must be documented transparently to avoid confusing external reviewers.

35. Conclusion

This comprehensive technical audit establishes that PRW-Wild is a functional, highly structured cyber-physical platform combining physical dual-ESP32 IoT sensing hardware, a robust Python digital twin backend, genuine ONNX deep learning vision inference, and an advanced WebGL Three.js interactive 3D simulation.

The repository exhibits exemplary engineering rigor in automated verification (139 / 139 passing tests), hardware failsafes (fail-closed piezoelectric safety gate), and strict state isolation between physical telemetry and virtual simulation state. By clearly delineating verified physical bench reality from simulated models and planned camera integrations, this document provides an unassailable technical foundation for future research publications, project presentations, and field deployment initiatives.

36. Technical Glossary

Term / AbbreviationFull Engineering Definition
CSIChannel State Information: Subcarrier-level amplitude and phase measurements in Wi-Fi OFDM communications used to detect dielectric body disturbance.
PIRPassive Infrared: Pyroelectric sensor measuring differential infrared radiation emitted by warm-blooded mammals.
I2SInter-IC Sound: Synchronous serial bus protocol designed specifically for communicating digital audio data between microcontrollers and MEMS transducers.
LoRaLong Range: Proprietary spread-spectrum radio frequency modulation technique based on Chirp Spread Spectrum (CSS) technology.
PDRPacket Delivery Ratio: The percentage of successfully received RF packets relative to the total number of transmitted packets.
FSMFinite State Machine: Computational model consisting of a finite number of states, transitions, and operating modes.
ONNXOpen Neural Network Exchange: Open format built to represent machine learning models, executed locally via ONNX Runtime.
PBRPhysically Based Rendering: Computer graphics rendering approach that models the realistic flow of light based on physical surface principles.
GLBBinary glTF: Compact binary file format for 3D scenes and models containing node hierarchies, meshes, materials, and skeletal animations.
